nfl.oneThing: The trade deadline is November 10, and the Ravens and Eagles are potentially searching for help. The Steelers are reportedly interested in Jets receiver Garrett Wilson.

headlines.title: Trade deadline is November 10
headlines.summary: Teams are starting to look for help before the deadline. CBS Sports has ranked 10 quarterbacks who could be available, with Mac Jones and Kirk Cousins at the top. The Ravens and Eagles are potentially in the market. The Steelers are reportedly interested in Jets receiver Garrett Wilson.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Ravens are 4–4 and one game behind the last AFC playoff spot, so their quarterback search matters for their season.

headlines.title: Lamar Jackson out after thumb surgery
headlines.summary: Lamar Jackson is out with a right thumb injury that requires surgery. Backup Tyler Huntley also went down in Sunday's loss to the Bills. Baltimore has added QB Austin Reed to the practice squad. The Ravens have lost three straight games and are 4–4.
headlines.whyItMatters: Baltimore is now working with a much thinner quarterback group while sitting just outside the AFC playoff picture.

headlines.title: Jack Campbell still in hospital
headlines.summary: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell remains in hospital for evaluation and monitoring of a neck injury suffered against the Vikings. The team says 'preliminary indications are positive'. Lions coach Dan Campbell called Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell a 'class act' for his actions after the injury.
headlines.whyItMatters: Detroit is 5–2 and fifth in the NFC, so updates on Campbell, a key defender, will be the main thing to watch.

headlines.title: Aiyuk hires Rosenhaus, wants back in NFL
headlines.summary: Brandon Aiyuk has hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, who says he is working on getting Aiyuk back to work and playing in the NFL. Aiyuk has not played since October 20, 2024, when he tore his right ACL, MCL and meniscus. The 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December after he stopped attending the facility.
headlines.whyItMatters: Aiyuk must apply for reinstatement before he can play again, and the 49ers would then decide what to do with his rights.

headlines.title: Colts stick with Daniel Jones
headlines.summary: Coach Shane Steichen says Daniel Jones will start Week 9 against the Cowboys, despite a 42–7 loss to the Jaguars. Jones threw two more interceptions, taking his season total to nine. His 39.6 QBR is the second-worst of his eight seasons. Steichen says the offence's problems go beyond Jones.
headlines.whyItMatters: Indianapolis is 2–6 and has lost four straight, so the quarterback decision will shape the rest of its season.

headlines.title: Lendeborg's start has the Warriors rethinking
headlines.summary: Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored 37 points with six threes in the Warriors' 124–112 win over the Clippers. Steve Kerr took him out with two minutes to play, after the Clippers cut a 21-point lead to eight. Lendeborg had been chasing 40 points. Golden State is 4–3, and CBS Sports calls his start one of the most impressive in NBA history.
headlines.whyItMatters: If the rookie keeps this up, it could change how the Warriors plan their season.

headlines.title: Grizzlies are the only unbeaten team
headlines.summary: Memphis is 6–0 after six straight wins and is the only team in the league still unbeaten. The Grizzlies lead the NBA in net rating at +15.1 after two weeks, ahead of Houston, Portland, Minnesota and Boston. Yahoo Sports notes they tore down their core over the summer.
headlines.whyItMatters: Memphis sits first in the West, and a 6–0 start with that net rating puts them in a strong early position.

headlines.title: Thunder to retire Westbrook's No. 0
headlines.summary: The Thunder will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0 on February 7, when they host the Knicks. Westbrook played the first 11 of his 18 seasons in Oklahoma City, won MVP and averaged a triple-double in three straight seasons. The game and ceremony will air on NBC and stream on Peacock.

teamNews.title: Spurs 4–2 and winning
